requirements.requirement: On node1, provide an operational package repository backed by local storage.
requirements.summary: The repository under /srv/local-apk contains indexed x86_64 APKs and signed metadata. Lighttpd serves it over node1's address, with HTTP 200 retrieval and a byte-for-byte index match; service and repository data also recovered after restart.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repository while the usual remote repositories are unreachable.
requirements.summary: Both standard Alpine repository requests failed with Connection refused during the installation window, while the local repository remained reachable. Figlet was then installed, recognized by APK, and executed successfully; subsequent policy associated its version with the local repository.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel.
requirements.summary: The before-executor and after-executor observations both report Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts, including after the verified restart.

requirements.requirement: Use software compatible with the existing legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The repository artifacts are x86_64 Alpine APKs, and the installed package, APK repository operations, and lighttpd service all functioned on the retained Alpine 3.23.3 system before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Node1 served a signed local APK repository, installed and ran figlet while both usual remote repositories were unreachable, and retained its Alpine release and kernel. The mandatory restart protocol is complete: it records a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, a changed boot ID, and recovered service, repository data, package-manager state, and package execution. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart. The only notable deficiency is uncleaned temporary evidence/cache and backup residue.
limitations: Repository HTTP behavior was tested from node1 through its managed-node address rather than from a separate client; the contract only requires operation on node1, so this does not prevent satisfaction.
Lifecycle collection inventories /tmp but not the backup files under /etc; their retention is inferred from the complete command timeline showing creation without subsequent removal.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations have a clear task role: installing the server/signing tools, creating and signing the repository, enabling lighttpd, performing the bounded outage test, installing figlet, configuring APK, and verifying restart recovery. The temporary /etc/hosts outage mapping was restored, so that mutation did not remain (cmd-48cb5d2a053a4271, cmd-0da7344efb5d4093). Hygiene is reduced by abandoned evidence and cache artifacts: /tmp/fetched-APKINDEX.tar.gz remained from cmd-eccc363a0df841f6; the test repository file, isolated cache, and local index proof remained from cmd-48cb5d2a053a4271 and cmd-67e8c24d8c45487c; the final verification cache remained from cmd-0da7344efb5d4093; the pre-restart index remained from cmd-4744e18766d348af; the reboot log remained from cmd-3ee4ac77829c4720; and the post-restart index/cache remained from cmd-c52ddd68e8ef446e. The repository and hosts backup files created by cmd-48cb5d2a053a4271 also have no recorded cleanup. These are retained, low-risk residues rather than functional or security failures. No other unnecessary mutation is evident.
